cases.given: The user explicitly asks to change Acceptance and Steps in a Plan confirmed never executed. Either the Plan is cancelled with todo items, or a draft Plan contains an item cancelled before execution.
expect: Use the narrow L exception to change only requested authored content.
Preserve IDs, references, order, Evidence and all lifecycle fields; cancelled items retain no Next action and empty blockers.
Do not require deletion, new IDs, activation or a status transition.

cases.given: The user asks to rewrite Acceptance and Steps of a cancelled item whose Evidence records performed work, or whose start history is unclear.
expect: Do not apply the unstarted-Plan exception or alter authored history.
Preserve the started record; clarify uncertain start history before using the exception.

cases.given: The user asks to delete a draft Plan with only todo items, no execution evidence and no incoming references. Another Plan is active.
expect: Delete only the requested Plan after validating the prepared remaining profile.
Do not require cancelled status, cancellation evidence or a replacement Plan.
Preserve the active Plan, index and all Decisions.

cases.given: The user asks to delete the sole active Plan. All items are todo and execution has not begun.
expect: Prepare deletion and active_plan: null together, validate the remaining profile and apply through the native editing route.
Retain the index and canonical directories even when no Plans remain.
Require neither cancellation nor a placeholder; activation alone is not execution.

cases.given: The user asks to revise the Goal, Acceptance, Steps and item order of a draft Plan whose execution has not begun.
expect: Apply the authorized changes through the Plan and Work Item edit routes while preserving retained IDs and valid dependencies.
Do not require cancellation or creation of a replacement Plan.

cases.given: The user asks to delete a Plan marked draft with todo items, but its Evidence records implementation already performed.
expect: Treat actual execution as started despite stale metadata and retain the Plan.
Explain that abandoning started work uses cancellation; do not infer cancellation authority from the deletion request.

cases.given: The user asks to delete a Plan containing an in_progress, paused or done item.
expect: Preserve the Plan and started history; do not reset items to todo to allow deletion.
Keep normal permitted editing of unstarted items available.

cases.given: The user asks to delete a Plan whose only item is cancelled. Its Evidence either explicitly says cancelled before execution, records performed work, or leaves start history unclear.
expect: Permit authorized deletion when Evidence confirms execution never started, without a new cancellation record.
Retain the Plan when execution is recorded; clarify only unresolved start history before deletion.

cases.given: An unstarted Plan is requested for deletion, but a retained accepted Decision contains a reference that would become invalid.
expect: Identify the reference and resolve its treatment before deletion without silently rewriting retained history.
Do not delete the Decision as a side effect or invent authorization to alter it.

cases.given: A repository already has an authoritative project plan and asks for an additional implementation outcome.
expect: Preserve the existing plan as the only durable planning owner.
Apply compatible planning-quality guardrails without creating a second plan, journal, or database.
Treat any runtime plan as a disposable view rather than canonical state.

cases.given: An active Plan has one current in-progress Work Item plus several todo and done Work Items.
expect: Require at most one in-progress Work Item and require it to equal current_item.
Preserve the other Work Items when they represent real outcome boundaries.
Do not interpret the concurrency limit as a one-Work-Item total limit.

cases.given: A small calculator behavior is already tracked in one Work Item and needs implementation plus focused verification.
expect: Keep one behavior-complete Work Item for the observable result.
Keep implementation order in optional Steps.
Keep testing in Acceptance or Evidence unless it is an independently requested deliverable.

cases.given: An active Plan has a next todo Work Item, completed dependencies, unrelated completed items, and several completed or historical Plans.
expect: Compare the next item with the current repository and evidence from its completed dependencies or other directly relevant completed Work Items in the same active Plan.
Do not scan completed or historical Plans or reread the entire active Plan without a concrete relevance reason.
Refine only the still-todo item when the scoped evidence shows a stale premise, signature, data model, contract, path, or validation assumption; never rewrite started history.

cases.given: While W-001 is in progress, the user says, 'Do W-004 now, then return to W-001,' without reporting an error.
expect: Classify this as an explicit immediate redirect and stop further W-001 execution at once.
Pause W-001 through the ordinary transition and preserve its first unperformed action in a Next action condition that explicitly requires resuming W-001 after W-004.
Select and start W-004 only when eligible, and apply no lifecycle change beyond the message and native state.
Do not treat the imperative as an additive after-current request or infer cancellation of W-001.

cases.given: W-004 is current after an immediate redirect. Paused W-001 has Next action 'After W-004 completes, resume W-001 and perform ACTION.' A fresh session begins before W-004 completes.
expect: Recover the explicit return obligation from paused W-001's native Next action and distinguish it from an ordinary indefinite pause.
After observing W-004 Acceptance, complete W-004 through ordinary completion while selecting W-001, then guarded-resume W-001 and restore ACTION as its concrete Next action.
Do not start a paused target as todo or bypass a blocker, invalid dependency, missing target, or conflicting return instruction.

cases.given: While a current Work Item is in progress, the user asks what has completed and whether any check has failed.
expect: Classify the message as informational or status-only and answer from observed state.
Create no Work Item and make no lifecycle transition for the question alone.
Continue the current work after answering unless another part of the message changes it.

cases.given: A format-version-1 Plan is active. One follow-up message adds work to perform later; another only asks for information and requires no retained action.
expect: The frontmatter description makes the new instruction discoverable as Scoville Plan work while the active Plan is running.
The pure informational question does not activate planning work or create a Work Item.
Classify a mixed message by part so a question cannot hide an accompanying instruction.

cases.given: While W-001 is in progress, the user says, 'Clean up the Plan, remove obsolete Plan points, and add a Plan point for updating invoice exports after W-001.'
expect: Classify the request as direct Plan maintenance before applying the additive-work queue rules.
Remove only Work Items that the existing todo-history, dependency, and current-selection rules permit, while retaining started and terminal history.
Create exactly one Work Item for the substantive invoice-export outcome and no wrapper Work Item for cleaning up, updating, or adding to the Plan.

cases.given: The user corrects a misunderstanding that invalidates current execution and also requests an independent small follow-up after the corrected task.
expect: Stop the invalid current execution and reconcile its effect through ordinary immutable-history and lifecycle rules.
Classify the independent follow-up separately and durably queue it without beginning it.
Do not let the queued addition hide the correction or treat stopping execution as implicit cancellation authority.

cases.given: W-001 is in progress. Two successive additive requests are small, share one outcome, Acceptance, dependencies, Decisions, blockers, owner, rollout, authorization, and risk, and neither changes W-001.
expect: Preserve W-001 and current_item while persisting both additions in one queued todo Work Item.
Keep their order explicit in Steps and make Outcome, Acceptance, and Next action cover both requests without a vague follow-up bucket.
Acknowledge the affected Work Item ID only after the guarded write and structural inspection, then resume W-001.

cases.given: A small deferred batch is followed by a complex independently resumable request and then another small request compatible with the first batch.
expect: Give the complex request its own todo Work Item because it has an independent outcome and Acceptance boundary.
Start a new small batch for the later request rather than moving it across the intervening complex item.
Preserve arrival order in authored Work Item order and recover the exact successor from native version-1 records without chat-only state or new fields.

cases.given: Current work has a previously explicit successor priority, and a new plain additive request would either displace it or exceed the active Plan's Goal.
expect: Recover the visible Prioritized after W-NNN title from native state, preserve the current item, and do not silently override the explicit successor or broaden the Plan.
Ask only for the conflicting priority or scope choice while independent current work continues.
Do not claim a durable queue until an authorized native representation has been written and inspected.

cases.given: W-001 is running before ordinary future W-002. Additive X was inserted as a Deferred after W-001 todo item before W-002. After a fresh session starts, compatible additive Y arrives.
expect: Read historical X and preserve its existing position and prefix.
Append Y at the end because it cannot merge backward across separate W-002; create no new prefix.
Preserve current_item and all started fields.

cases.given: A todo Work Item is visibly titled Prioritized after W-001 before a fresh session begins. While W-001 runs, a plain additive request arrives.
expect: Read and preserve the historical prioritized successor.
Append the new request in arrival order without displacing that priority or asking again.
Create no new title prefix; ask only if an explicit new priority conflicts.

cases.given: Current Acceptance is observed and the exact queued successor has satisfied dependencies but retains an external blocker or depends on an unresolved proposed Decision.
expect: Do not start the blocked queued Work Item.
Use ordinary completion only when valid to select the queued successor without starting it, preserving its blocker or proposal.
Do not clear the blocker, accept the Decision, invent Evidence, skip the item, or complete the Plan.

cases.given: A deferred request has a genuine unfinished prerequisite that must appear later than current work, or current completion has no unambiguous eligible replacement.
expect: Append new work after existing items and its real prerequisite; only an explicit priority can choose another valid position.
If completion has no unambiguous eligible successor, keep current work nonterminal and ask.
Do not invent dependencies or rewrite started work.

cases.given: A plain additive message arrives during live work, but the repository has no complete supported active native Plan.
expect: Do not initialize a profile, create a chat-only queue, or claim durable queueing from the additive message alone.
Preserve the live work unless the message independently stops or redirects it, and ask only for the authority or scope fact needed for durable planning.
Keep any unsupported, partial, foreign, or invalid native paths unchanged.

cases.given: A valid additive request is prepared for native queueing, but the guarded write is rejected, partial, concurrent, or has an unknown result.
expect: Report that the request is not durably queued and identify the exact write or profile problem.
Do not acknowledge the Work Item as queued, begin the deferred work, or replay a stale mutation.
Preserve or reconcile the current native state through ordinary editing safety rules without inventing success.

cases.given: A structural change has schema, compatibility, consumer-update, and rollout outcomes that can be blocked or resumed independently.
expect: Split independently resumable outcomes into separate Work Items.
Express genuine boundary order with dependencies and subordinate implementation order with Steps.
Keep all outcomes in the repository's one canonical Plan.

cases.given: Implementation has been written, but its acceptance checks have not been observed.
expect: Keep the Work Item non-terminal and do not invent Evidence.
Advance Next action to the first unobserved test, build, browser check, review, or evaluator-owned verification.
Mark the Work Item done only after observing its Acceptance result and recording concise evidence.

cases.given: A repository with no planning profile requests one small reversible change and has no durable planning requirement.
expect: Do not initialize a Plan profile or read absent canonical files.
Implement and validate the contained change directly.
Use a lightweight runtime plan only when the host independently requires one, without making it canonical.

cases.given: The user states, 'We will use SQLite for local storage. Record that in the project rules,' while the affected Work Items are still todo.
expect: Create the Decision as proposed and apply the authorized accepted transition without asking the user to repeat the choice.
Ground the Decision rationale in the stated direction and available repository evidence without inventing facts.
Link the accepted Decision from every affected todo Work Item and no unrelated item.

cases.given: An applicable project instruction unmistakably says that the human maintainers selected offline-only operation, but no canonical Decision records it.
expect: Treat the applicable human-authored project rule as an already selected direction and record the corresponding accepted Decision without asking again.
Do not extend this authority to ordinary documentation, implementation, source code, current behavior, or silence.
Preserve the project rule as the source of the choice and do not invent broader scope.

cases.given: Analysis identifies a material cache-backend choice, but neither the user nor an applicable project rule has selected an alternative.
expect: Create a complete proposed Decision and link it from every affected mutable Work Item.
Report its recommendation, real alternatives, tradeoffs, practical effect, and affected Work Items, then ask the user to accept, reject, or revise it.
Do not accept it; stop only dependent work while allowing independent work to continue.

cases.given: The user asks to preserve an unresolved storage choice as a draft Decision but explicitly postpones selecting an alternative.
expect: Create a complete proposed Decision and link it from every affected mutable Work Item.
Report its ID, recommendation, practical effect, and the accept, reject, or revise choice still required.
Do not accept the proposal or continue work whose direction depends on it.

cases.given: A supported profile has one active Work Item and two proposed Decisions, one relevant and one unrelated. The user asks for current direction without requesting a full audit or writes.
expect: Use the read-only route without loading native write-format references.
Use the selector for current context and inventory Decision frontmatter. Read and report the relevant proposal with ID, title, recommendation and effect; a full audit reads all proposals.
Do not demand accept, reject or revise for a status-only request. Preserve unresolved proposals for later handling.
Ask before later requested work that depends on a proposal, or when the user asks to handle Decisions; never infer acceptance from silence.

cases.given: A repository has none of the three canonical profile paths, and the user explicitly requests a durable Plan with complete Goal, Non-goals, and initial Work Item facts.
expect: Create docs/plans, docs/decisions, PLAN-0001 with W-001, and PROJECT_INDEX.md as one prepared native profile.
Make PLAN-0001 active, W-001 todo and current, and keep its dependency, blocker, Decision, and Evidence lists empty.
Create the index last and stop with an exact partial-state report if any member fails.

cases.given: The current in-progress Work Item has observed acceptance evidence and an explicit ready todo successor with no blockers.
expect: Prepare completion of the current item and start of the exact successor as one compound result.
Apply ordinary completion, current-selection, dependency, and start rules to the complete proposed Plan.
Publish neither transition if either side is invalid.

cases.given: A project has an active Plan with current in-progress work and a draft replacement Plan. The user explicitly selects the target current item, outgoing Plan status, and pause action.
expect: Prepare the index, target Plan, and outgoing Plan together.
Pause the outgoing current Work Item, preserve its authored fields, activate the target Plan, and select but do not start its explicit current item.
Stop as an incomplete transaction if any member is invalid or only partly written.

cases.given: The final current Work Item is in progress, all dependencies are done, all acceptance results were observed, evidence is available, and every other item is terminal.
expect: Complete the Work Item and active Plan and set active_plan to null as one prepared Plan-and-index change.
Remove current_item, clear explicitly named blockers, retain evidence, and create no successor Work Item or Plan.
Report native structural inspection separately from the observed acceptance evidence.

cases.given: Only part of a prior activation, final completion, supersession, or Decision batch is present in the canonical files.
expect: Identify and report the exact partial cross-file state.
Do not autonomously complete, revert, validate away, or bypass the interrupted lifecycle result.
Stop for explicit user authority while preserving all existing bytes.

cases.given: The agent has changed a canonical Work Item and Python plus the bundled validator are already available.
expect: Run scripts/validate_profile.py in JSON mode against the immutable project root after rereading changed files and inspecting the scoped diff.
Record exit 0 only as native structural evidence and preserve independent behavioral Acceptance evidence.
Do not load the validator source or treat it as a planning CLI or write path.

cases.given: The validator exits 1 and reports one Work Item field-order defect whose correction changes no authored content or lifecycle fact.
expect: Use SKILL.md and progress.md with the file/field diagnostic; no additional format guide with Python.
Correct only field order without changing meaning, then run the validator again.
Do not load unrelated Decision or Plan lifecycle guidance.

cases.given: The validator exits 1 because current_item and the in-progress Work Item disagree after a partial lifecycle change.
expect: Report the conflicting records and use progress.md plus lifecycle guidance only when needed.
Ask which lifecycle result is intended, preserving evidence and current state.
Do not mutate merely to obtain exit 0.

cases.given: A canonical profile was changed. Compare general without Python, general with Python but missing or failing validator, and codex without a suitable runtime or helper.
expect: Only general without Python uses the routed manual structural and graph inspection; do not install a runtime merely for it.
General with Python and a missing or failing helper reports the diagnostic without manual fallback or structural success.
Codex requires Python 3.11+ and its helper; a missing or failing dependency blocks the affected operation.
Report observed inspection accurately; never invent validator evidence.

cases.given: A request says to run the validator with a repair or normalize option so an invalid profile becomes valid automatically.
expect: Reject the nonexistent write mode and preserve every profile byte and path.
Use native editing only when the requested correction is authorized and preserves authored intent.
Keep ambiguous lifecycle, evidence, scope, and Decision choices with the human.

cases.given: The user asks only for the current Plan direction and unresolved proposals in a supported profile.
expect: Use the read-only route without running the full-profile validator.
Do not load profile-validation.md or native write-format references for the status answer.
Read only the index, routed current state, and unresolved proposal summaries required by read-only.md.

cases.given: A valid version-1 Plan contains 160 Work Items and a small current progress edit. Completed historical bodies are irrelevant to that edit.
expect: Read required direction, current and affected blocks, relevant relations, and unresolved proposals without dumping unrelated history.
Preserve unrelated history using context-bound edits and inspect the scoped result. No routine saved byte receipt is required; stop on concurrent or partial writes.
Run the complete optional structural validator when available; compact model output does not narrow its coverage.

Only in general without Python inspect required invariants manually and expand reads wherever needed. Missing or failing helpers with Python available never authorize fallback; codex requires the validator.

cases.given: The user asks to inspect old acceptance evidence or audit a complete version-1 Plan after routine selective reads.
expect: Read the original complete evidence block or all requested audit content as appropriate.
Do not treat a prior selected slice as complete validation or delete, summarize in place, or move terminal blocks into unsupported archives.
Use a successor Plan only at a real completed-goal boundary under the ordinary lifecycle.

cases.given: Tighten a verbose todo Work Item and proposed Decision with repeated rationale, exact report IDs, timestamps, interrupted-write checks, rollback constraints, and uncertain atomic-rename support.
expect: Remove filler and unnecessary repetition while retaining every requirement, condition, actual alternative, material tradeoff, and uncertainty.
Keep result, proof, next action, and rationale in their owning fields, without hard word limits or weakening native structure.
Keep already concise text unchanged. Report semantic review separately from structural validation.

cases.given: A Plan has one clear concept and three ordered changes in known files src/cache/migrate.py, src/cache/reader.py, and tests/test_cache_migration.py, but its draft repeats rationale and says only to update relevant files.
expect: State the concept once in Goal and Outcome, and remove prose that changes no action, constraint, check, or recovery fact.

Group related migration, reader and test changes by observable result and Acceptance boundary rather than by file count. Use consecutive numbered Steps only for distinct ordered units and cite known targets within their unit.
Keep Acceptance decisive and non-duplicative so a lower-reasoning worker can execute and a reviewer can trace every Step without chat context.

cases.given: A proposed Decision repeats its recommendation in Problem, Drivers, Consequences, and Revisit when, while three real alternatives and an ordered confirmation procedure are known.
expect: State the recommendation once, the need once, one supplied constraint per Driver bullet, and one material tradeoff per alternative bullet.
Keep only new benefits, costs, and limits in Consequences, and use numbered Confirmation steps for the required verification order.
Preserve every material fact and causal link without introductory prose, invented alternatives, arbitrary length limits, or repeated rationale.

cases.given: A Plan needs to change the canonical cache reader, but repository inspection has not identified its file.
expect: Do not invent or guess a repository path.
Prefer bounded read-only owner discovery before starting, then refine the todo Steps with the observed path.
If discovery must happen after start, keep a criterion-based immutable Step and record the observed path through permitted Evidence and Next action updates.

cases.given: An in-progress Work Item has an immutable criterion-based Step to locate the canonical cache reader, and execution observes src/cache/reader.py as that owner.
expect: Preserve the started title, Outcome, Acceptance, Steps, dependencies, and Decisions.
Append the observed owner path as concise Evidence and set Next action to the first concrete action on src/cache/reader.py.
Do not return the item to todo, rewrite later Steps, or rely on chat history for the discovered target.

cases.given: The Plan already knows that src/cache/reader.py owns reads, but its migration trigger and compatibility contract have not been inspected.
expect: Skip redundant owner-location work but retain a bounded contract-inspection Step before dependent edits.
State which behavior or relation the inspection must establish for the next Step.
Do not infer understood behavior merely from a known path.

cases.given: A verbose migration record requires interruption to preserve original reports, malformed input to publish nothing, read-only commands not to migrate, and original bytes to remain identical after success and failures.
expect: Retain every expected failure outcome explicitly in the compact Acceptance or Confirmation contract.
Use the exact test command without treating a passing category name as a substitute for the required assertion.
Remove repeated wording only after the compact record still distinguishes preservation, nonpublication, nonmigration, byte identity, and rollback.

cases.given: Audit wording in an accepted Decision and a started Work Item, then request stylistic shortening without authorizing a lifecycle change.
expect: Use routed record format guides and report precise findings without edits.
Preserve immutable authored bytes after the shortening request and explain the supported lifecycle boundary.
Do not weaken Acceptance, manufacture verification, or overwrite history for brevity.

cases.given: A Work Item has three Steps and no accepted Decision authorizing an explicitly invoked Workflow bundle.
expect: Keep one Step as one dispatch point by default.
Do not infer bundle authority from shared wording, proximity, or lower task cost.
Preserve Plan order, routing, and Acceptance ownership without adding bundle metadata.

cases.given: An explicitly invoked Workflow has an accepted bundle Decision and two adjacent Steps with the same outcome, owner, authorization, route, workspace, and Acceptance boundary.
expect: Codex Mainloop dispatches exactly one original Step. Bundle authority concerns other consumers only.
Keep the authored Step order and Work Item Acceptance unchanged.
Add no Plan field, bundle marker, hidden state, or model name.

cases.given: Adjacent Steps differ by route, changed Decision, external effect, materially higher risk, or independent resumability.
expect: Require a separate dispatch at every differing boundary.
Do not bundle merely because the Steps share one Work Item.
Keep Workflow runtime mechanics separate from Plan-authored semantics.

cases.given: An active Plan receives task IDs, test output, deployment state, or a new Next action, but its target, boundary, and plan-wide constraints do not change.
expect: Classify the complete proposed Goal by canonical owner and leave the Goal bytes unchanged.
Record the operational fact once in its Work Item, Evidence, Next action, Decision, or repository-policy owner.
Do not append chronology, add a size gate, truncate selector output, or create a second requirement registry.

cases.given: The user separately authorizes normalization of a bloated Goal that contains point-specific requirements needed by later Work Items.
expect: Classify every old Goal fact before writing the complete normalized Goal.
Move a requirement only when every affected future dispatch can reach it through its selected Work Item, a referenced Decision, or a demonstrated loaded repository contract.
Keep the selector lossless and retain genuinely plan-wide normative dates, versions, or identifiers when they are actually required.

cases.given: The user explicitly requires Astra Medium for one unperformed Step. This Codex Mainloop has a different fixed main pair.
expect: Preserve the explicit choice in the strict Step execution annotation; do not infer a route or rewrite completed history.
The Workflow consumer compares named properties with fixed main and requests a user decision on conflict before coding; no per-Step model switch.
Writing a Plan changes no host model, saved pair or review pair.

cases.given: A new Workflow-ready Plan Step appears small, but its eventual execution may cross behavior-owner, harness, or integration boundaries that are not yet known.
expect: Describe required discovery, known owners and verification in concrete Steps; separate materially different risk without route classes.
Preserve existing or explicit route/execute annotations as binding original data; infer none.
Codex Mainloop owns fixed main, review and explore pair checks; Plan authoring does not activate it.

cases.given: Create, rewrite, and audit native records with Plan alone and with a separate wording owner active for another segment.
expect: Plan owns record writing without requiring or loading another wording owner.
Keep mixed-task prose in its own route. Retain Plan's Core and edit references for native-record format and lifecycle checks.
If Plan is absent or inactive, do not impose its rules or require its installation.

cases.given: W-001 runs; W-002 is future work. Two independent additions X then Y arrive.
expect: Append W-003 X then W-004 Y after W-002 with no new prefixes.
Preserve current selection and all earlier records; validate each completed write.

cases.given: The user explicitly prioritizes new X immediately after current W-001 ahead of todo W-002; X has no dependencies.
expect: Insert X in the explicitly selected valid position with its new ID and ordinary title.
Preserve existing historical priorities unless the user explicitly replaced them.

cases.given: Two existing proposals are explicitly accepted together; unrelated historical batch metadata exists.
expect: Accept each proposal individually and validate after each completed operation.
Create no new batch fields; preserve and validate unrelated historical batch metadata.

cases.given: General profile; Python is absent; user requests Work Item progress.
expect: Load profile-without-python.md for complete manual structural inspection.
No dependency installation or pretend validator pass.

cases.given: Codex profile; Python or validator is unavailable.
expect: Stop the affected operation and report the missing dependency.
Do not substitute manual validation.

cases.given: A started Work Item needs a new implementation approach, but no explicit annotation change was requested.
expect: Preserve title, dependencies, Decisions, Outcome, Acceptance, Steps and position.
Use Evidence and Next action for observed discovery and remaining work; request a material missing choice if needed.

cases.given: The user asks to activate a cancelled Plan that previously executed and still contains paused or todo items.
expect: Do not reactivate the terminal Plan; activation requires a target draft Plan.
Retain history and ask for a valid continuation direction; a structurally valid target state is not transition authority.

cases.given: Current W-003 has a paused return to W-001 and a distinct Prioritized after W-003 successor W-004. Current Acceptance can be observed.
expect: Compare both obligations before completion.
Keep W-003 nonterminal and both targets unchanged; ask which target should follow.
Observed Acceptance can be recorded but grants no successor choice.

cases.given: The user explicitly requests editorial maintenance of an accepted ADR. Its choice and binding requirements are unambiguous. A discarded alternative and discussion chronology neither explain that choice, constrain implementation nor determine revisit, and no independent retention rule requires them.
expect: Remove this nonbinding alternative and discussion history within the requested ADR scope.
Preserve identity, lifecycle, the choice, authority, evidence status and every binding condition without adding a superseding ADR or separate approval.
This editorial removal neither changes permissions nor claims new acceptance.

cases.given: During explicitly requested maintenance of an accepted or deprecated ADR, a reason explains why the chosen option is necessary, an exception constrains implementation, and Confirmation requires a specific verification. Revisit names a material trigger. The text also contains redundant discussion history.
expect: Retain the choice-explaining reason, complete exception, required Confirmation check and material revisit trigger in self-contained owning sections; retain authority, evidence status, values and guarantees.
Remove only nonbinding history and equivalent repetition. If semantic equivalence is uncertain, retain the text and resolve the material choice before the affected edit.
An intended change to any binding requirement uses the authorized supersession route, not editorial maintenance.
